extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in international/political news
extracted.subtask_description: A multi-item front-page newspaper report compiling wire-service and staff dispatches on international diplomacy, war-crime trials, occupation policy directives, and human-interest incidents. Content is typical of mid-20th-century daily newspapers presenting factual accounts and official statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only read portions of documents are evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: “the court has ruled that only the parts of documents which are actually read in court would be considered evidence in the record.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jackson had intended to outline document contents and let the court consider them full, but the court’s ruling that only parts actually read count has slowed the procedure. Affidavits, by contrast, often take only two minutes to present—illustrating a time tradeoff between reading documents verbatim and using affidavits or summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document selection / trimming for trial presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: “one United States attorney had 200 documents which he considered essential to his presentation. Jackson ordered the number cut to 38. Then he ordered it cut again.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecutors must balance thoroughness and speed: the U.S. prosecution aims to present a full picture but is anxious for speed; the British prosecution favors ‘weeding out detail’ to cover more ground quickly. Judges may demand strict limits on the volume of documents presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction for trials of lesser German generals
rubrics_metrics.description: “When the trials of the lesser generals come, they will be on a zonal rather than an international basis with each power trying those it had in custody in its zone of occupation.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrangement is a procedural rule for venue/authority: lower‑rank defendants captured by a particular occupying power will be tried by that power in its zone rather than by the multinational tribunal. Officials expressed doubt over handing suspects back to German courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Censor's stamp required on stories for transmission abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: “All stories written for transmission abroad, no matter what their source or subject, must have the censor’s stamp.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Soviet and other occupation censors handled advance stories; censorship policy has been relaxed and tightened at times. The requirement affects what foreign correspondents can transmit and can delay or alter the flow of news. The Associated Press had not tested the tightened censorship at the time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on officers talking to newsmen / advance operational information
rubrics_metrics.description: “Restrictions that prohibited officers from talking to newsmen had been removed... the only restriction in effect recently has been against officers' giving advance operational information.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Military-imposed limits on officer-comment are a form of press control: correspondents said the curb prevented them from getting news. Restrictions may be applied or lifted depending on security concerns; when lifted, correspondents can again confer with officers but may still be barred from operational details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allied directive on State Shinto — three-point program
rubrics_metrics.description: The Allied directive laid down a program of broad revision, calling for: 1. Withdrawal of all Government control and support of state Shinto—“the way of the gods.” 2. Purging of militaristic and ultra-nationalistic ideology from doctrine of the cult which preaches ancestor worship and defies the Emperor. 3. Removal of Shinto teachings from schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy aims to free people from direct or indirect compulsion to believe in a ‘manufactured’ religion and to dismantle state-sponsored ideological apparatus. Officials emphasized this applies to state Shinto (its government support and institutions) and is not intended to dictate private religious belief or to abolish sect Shinto.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal legal basis for all creeds; voluntary shrine support
rubrics_metrics.description: “All creeds, religions and faiths are placed upon exactly the same legal basis... ‘Shinto shrines that have a real religious following will be able to exist on voluntary contributions.’”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of separation of state and religion, government support/administration of shrines is to be removed; religious bodies may continue on voluntary funding. The directive frames freedom of religion as equal legal treatment rather than state endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emperor’s public religious role restricted (no state accompaniment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the Emperor may continue to worship at the Grand Shrine of Ise, in the future the Emperor cannot be accompanied by state officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This administrative constraint is part of removing state endorsement of shrine worship and ensures state officials do not perform or symbolize official sanction of religious rites; it separates ceremonial personal acts from state ceremony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence recovery obligation for prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations: suspects or their friends “destroyed, altered or secreted” incriminating documents; prosecution must “dig out everything we get,” including sending staff to Germany to obtain documents used in European war‑crime trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecutors face an evidentiary burden exacerbated by destroyed/hidden documents and national isolation; they may need to seek records across zones and from captured archives, and adapt presentation strategies to incomplete documentary records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of international war-crimes tribunal
rubrics_metrics.description: “The court will be made up of members from China, Great Britain and Russia as well as the United States.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tribunal’s multinational composition is a procedural standard determining judges/representation; this affects trial rules, evidence handling, and perceptions of legitimacy across occupied/joint jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for expanding Japanese fishing areas
rubrics_metrics.description: “Fishing areas available to Japanese fleets cannot be expanded unless the industry demonstrates it has exhausted every possible means to increase catches.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A regulatory test imposed by Supreme Allied Headquarters: expansion of access is conditional on demonstrable need and prior efforts to increase domestic production. The statement reflects an occupancy authority’s resource-allocation policy.
